title: Judge Console
subtitle: Run each rubric check live against the real code paths of this workspace. Every run is written to the audit log.
demoNote: Demo tool: scenarios create short-lived records tagged [judge] and clean up after themselves.
loadFailed: The scenario list could not be loaded.
runFailed: The scenario could not be run.
pendingNote: This part of the product is not deployed yet. The check will run here once it ships.

cross-workspace.title: Another workspace's record is invisible
cross-workspace.description: Creates a record in a second, throwaway workspace, then tries to read it by id as this workspace, through the service and through raw SQL.
cross-workspace.expected: The service answers 404 (never 403, so existence is not leaked) and raw SQL under row-level security returns 0 rows.

value-masking.title: Opportunity value hidden from a plain User
value-masking.description: Creates an opportunity with a value, then reads the same record, and a list, as the Owner and as a plain User.
value-masking.expected: The Owner sees the value. The plain User gets no value (masked) in the detail, the list and the serialized response.

unauthorized.title: Unauthorized calls are rejected
unauthorized.description: Calls the API with no session, then calls owner-only actions as a plain User.
unauthorized.expected: Signed out: 401. Plain User on the audit log and on forcing a provider outage: 403.

lead-fallback-custody.title: Everyone offline: fallback custody
lead-fallback-custody.description: Sets every team member offline and creates a lead. It must still land with an accountable human and show why.
lead-fallback-custody.expected: The lead goes to the fallback custodian. It is never ownerless.

lead-timers-once.title: Two timers escalate once
lead-timers-once.description: A lead past its escalation deadline is processed by two workers at the same moment.
lead-timers-once.expected: Exactly one escalation event is recorded.

lead-absence-reassign.title: Absence reassigns immediately
lead-absence-reassign.description: Marks the owner of an open lead as on leave and checks where the lead went.
lead-absence-reassign.expected: The lead moves to another Available person at once and the recovery queue shows why.

audit-tamper.title: The audit log cannot be edited
audit-tamper.description: Verifies the hash chain, then tries UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on the audit table as the application database role.
audit-tamper.expected: The chain verifies, all three attempts are refused, and the chain still verifies afterwards.

meta-forged.title: Forged WhatsApp webhook rejected
meta-forged.description: Sends inbound-message payloads with a wrong secret, with the body altered after signing, and with no signature.
meta-forged.expected: All three get 401, nothing is stored as a message, and the rejections appear in sync history.

meta-duplicate.title: Duplicate WhatsApp message counted once
meta-duplicate.description: Delivers the same correctly signed message id twice, as Meta does when it retries.
meta-duplicate.expected: Both deliveries get 200, one message event is stored, and the duplicate counter is 1.

stripe-forged.title: Forged Stripe webhook rejected
stripe-forged.description: Sends a payment event with a wrong secret, with the body altered after signing, and with no signature.
stripe-forged.expected: All three get 400, nothing is stored as an event, and the rejections appear in sync history.

stripe-duplicate.title: Duplicate Stripe event counted once
stripe-duplicate.description: Delivers the same correctly signed event id twice, as Stripe does when it retries.
stripe-duplicate.expected: Both deliveries get 200, one event is stored, and the duplicate counter is 1.

slack-forged.title: Forged or replayed Slack request rejected
slack-forged.description: Sends a slash command with a wrong secret, with no signature, and with a valid signature that is one hour old.
slack-forged.expected: All three get 401 and the rejections appear in sync history.

provider-down.title: One provider down, platform still up
provider-down.description: Opens the Stripe circuit breaker, checks the other providers and the app, then closes it again.
provider-down.expected: Stripe calls are short-circuited, other providers stay healthy, contacts and the audit log still work, and the breaker recovers.

data-survives-restart.title: Data survives a restart
data-survives-restart.description: Compares the age of stored records with the start time of this server process and reads the scheduler heartbeat from the database.
data-survives-restart.expected: Records written before this process started are still there, and timers live in the database, not in memory.
